newsitem.title: UK: Northern Ireland utility buys fuel to cover gas conversion.
newsitem.headline: Northern Ireland utility buys fuel to cover gas conversion.

text.p: Northern Ireland's generator Premier Power has bought more high sulphur fuel oil this winter for its Ballylunford power station than initially anticipated during its conversion to gas-burning, a company spokesman said on Monday.
"There have been a number of factors resulting in us buying about 75 percent more fuel than we expected, but the conversion schedule is still on track," said Premier Power's Sam Cunningham.
Premier is a unit of British Gas Plc.

It took deliver of 25,000 tonnes in November and will receive a further 50,000 tonnes this month. Some dealers in the fuel oil market were surprised by the utilities' purchase last week of a 25,000 tonne cargo.
"There has been some talk that maybe there's a problem (with the conversion to gas)," one fuel oil trader said.

But Premier's Cunningham said the extra material was primarily to cover for increased electricity demand resulting from colder weather and a cancelled supply contract from a coal-burning power station. Minor glitches and technical hiccups were also factors.
"We have not bought much compared with the 125,000 tonnes I estimate we would have needed if the plant was still running entirely on fuel," said Cunningham.
He added that it was not clear whether further spot purchases would be necessary.

Premier Power is converting its oil burning Ballylunford power station to gas. The facility took its first delivery of gas on October 1 via a 135 km pipeline from Dumfries and Galloway in southwest Scotland.
The company says its is 75 percent converted to gas and expects to have 100 percent conversion by the end of January.
Premier Power was one of Europe's largest end-users of high sulphur fuel oil, consuming around 900,000 tonnes a year out of a European total of 2.5 million tonnes.
